What We Design

Eight connected layers turn a showroom floor into a clear, confident brand experience.

01

Display Planning

Fixtures, sightlines and product groupings planned around how customers browse.

02

Customer Flow Design

A natural route from entrance to feature displays, decisions and checkout.

03

Brand Zone Design

Distinct zones communicate collections, campaigns and brand priorities clearly.

04

Product Lighting

Ambient and focused light reveal colour, texture and detail accurately.

05

Material & Finish Selection

Durable surfaces support the brand and hold up to daily footfall.

06

Trial & Demo Areas

Comfortable places to test, compare and understand products before buying.

07

Storage & Back-of-House

Stock, packing and staff functions stay efficient and out of customer sight.

08

Facade & Window Display

The storefront introduces the brand and gives people a reason to step inside.

01 / 08

Our Design Process

Five clear stages take the showroom from product brief to an approved visual package.

01

Consultation & Requirements

We review the product range, brand, customer profile, budget and opening target.

02

Site Measurement

We record the floor, frontage, services, access and existing conditions.

03

Concept & Layout Design

Display zones, sightlines and customer flow are tested together.

04

Material & Furniture Selection

Display fixtures, finishes and lighting are coordinated for daily use.

05

Final Design Package & 3D Visualization

Approved 3D views and drawings prepare the showroom for pricing and execution.

Showroom Design FAQs

Straight answers on sales, lighting, customer flow, leased spaces, timing and 3D approval.

A clear layout places priority products in stronger sightlines, makes comparison easier and guides customers naturally through the full range.

fields.heading: Showroom Design FAQs
fields.copy: Straight answers on sales, lighting, customer flow, leased spaces, timing and 3D approval.

items.q: How does showroom design help boost sales?
items.a: A clear layout places priority products in stronger sightlines, makes comparison easier and guides customers naturally through the full range.

items.q: What lighting is best for showroom products?
items.a: Layered lighting works best. Ambient light keeps the room comfortable, while adjustable spotlights reveal product colour, texture and detail.

items.q: How do you plan customer flow?
items.a: We study the entrance, key displays, decision points and checkout path, then create a route that feels natural without forcing movement.

items.q: Can you design a rented showroom?
items.a: Yes. We can prioritise modular displays, reversible finishes and landlord conditions for a leased space.

items.q: How long does showroom design take?
items.a: A focused showroom usually takes two to four weeks from survey to final design. Larger flagship spaces need a longer programme.

items.q: Will I see 3D visuals before execution?
items.a: Yes. Key customer views and display zones are shown in 3D so you can approve the experience before site work begins.
